resources.string: No screen reader is installed
There is no screen reader left on the phone, not even TalkBack. It can be reinstalled from the saved backup, with no Internet, or from the store.
%1$s is on but not responding
Android has %1$s turned on, but the service crashed and does not work. Restarting it, turning it off and on again, usually fixes it. If not, force stop it or reinstall it.
Two screen readers are on at once
These are on: %1$s. Two screen readers at once get in each other\'s way: they talk over each other or ignore gestures. Turn off the one you do not use.
No screen reader is on
No screen reader is on, so the phone does not speak. You can turn on %1$s now.
%1$s works
Turn on %1$s
With the advanced permission it turns on at once. Without it, I guide you through Settings and press the buttons once you confirm.
Turn off %1$s
Restart %1$s
Turns it off and on again.
Force stop %1$s
Closes the app completely. Android turns it off when doing so; then it is turned on again.
Checked: %1$s is on.
%1$s could not be turned on.
Checked: %1$s is off.
%1$s could not be turned off.
Checked: %1$s restarted and is running.
%1$s did not start again. Try force stopping it or reinstalling it.
Reinstall %1$s from the backup, version %2$s
No Internet needed. Android asks you to confirm; I read the dialog to you and press it if you confirm.
%1$s could not be reinstalled.
Accessible Rescue must be allowed to install apps. Turn on the switch on this screen and choose the option again.
Open %1$s in the store
To install or update it. Needs the Internet.
Store open at %1$s.
This phone has no app store. Use a saved backup or install the file from the app.
Google TalkBack is not installed
You use another screen reader. If it ever fails, TalkBack is the most common alternative: you can install it from a backup or the store.
There is no speech engine apart from the rescue voice
There is no system speech engine, such as Google\'s. Your screen reader can use the rescue voice built into this app, or you can reinstall Google\'s.
The chosen speech engine is no longer installed
The system speech engine is set to %1$s, which is no longer on the phone. Choose another engine or use the rescue voice.
%1$s is disabled
The speech engine %1$s is disabled, so it cannot speak. It must be enabled in its app info, or another engine chosen.
Enable %1$s
The speech rate or pitch is extreme
The system voice is at %1$d percent rate and %2$d percent pitch. Normal is 100. If it is hard to understand, set them to normal.
Set the rate and pitch to normal
Checked: system voice rate and pitch at 100 percent.
The rate and pitch could not be changed.
Speech settings open. Look for Speech rate and Pitch, and press Reset.
The speech engine
%1$s does not start
%1$s, the system speech engine, does not start. That is why your screen reader is silent. Use the rescue voice as the system voice or repair the engine.
%1$s has no voice in %2$s
%1$s starts, but the voice for the phone\'s language is not installed, or only works online. Install the voice or use another engine.
%1$s does not speak
%1$s starts but produces no sound. Your screen reader stays silent even though it is on. Use the rescue voice as the system voice, go back to the engine that worked, or repair this one.
The system voice works: %1$s
Rescue voice
Use the rescue voice as the system voice
The voice built into this app, with no Internet. Your screen reader speaks again with it.
Go back to %1$s, which worked
The last engine the rescue checked was speaking.
Checked: %1$s is now the system speech engine. If your screen reader is still silent, restart it.
%1$s could not be set as the speech engine.
Open the system speech settings
Speech settings open. Look for Preferred engine and choose another engine.
Install the voice for your language in %1$s
Opens the engine\'s voices screen. Downloading a voice needs the Internet.
Voices screen of %1$s open. Look for your language and download it.
%1$s has no screen to install voices. Use another engine.
Uninstall the updates of %1$s
Goes back to the factory version. Useful if it fails since it was updated.
Clear the cache of %1$s
The volume is too low
The screen reader voice volume is at %1$d percent and media at %2$d percent. Like this you may hear nothing.
Turn the volume up
Raises the accessibility and media volume to a level you can hear.
Checked: accessibility volume at %1$d percent and media at %2$d percent.
The volume is still low: accessibility at %1$d percent and media at %2$d percent. Turn it up with the keys while your screen reader speaks.
Bluetooth audio is connected: %1$s
Bluetooth headphones or a speaker can take the voice even when far away or in a pocket. If you are not wearing them, disconnect them. The rescue voice can always speak through the phone speaker.
Make the rescue voice always use the speaker
Done: the rescue voice will always speak through the phone speaker.
Open Bluetooth settings
Bluetooth settings open. Turn Bluetooth off or disconnect the device.
Wired headphones are detected
The phone thinks wired headphones are connected. If they are not, the socket may be dirty and the sound goes to it instead of the speaker.
The phone is on silent, vibrate or Do Not Disturb
It does not silence screen readers, but it does silence music, notifications and the voice of some apps.
The sound balance is far to one side
Almost all the sound comes out on one side. With headphones, you may not hear the voice in the other ear.
Accessibility settings open. Look for Audio, Hearing enhancements or Balance, and center the balance.
Mono audio is on
It is only a problem if you turned it on by mistake: it mixes both channels into one.
Accessibility settings open. Look for Mono audio and turn it off if you do not want it.
Open accessibility settings
%1$s is disabled
The app %1$s is disabled on the phone and cannot work. It must be enabled in its app info.
%1$s has updates installed
If %1$s started failing after an update, you can go back to the factory version by uninstalling its updates.
Other services on: %1$s
Accessibility services that are not screen readers but can take over touch or the keys, such as Switch Access. If you do not use them, turn them off.
This Android has no accessibility shortcut
The volume key shortcut came with Android 8. Open the rescue from the icon, the quick settings tile or the guardian.
The volume shortcut does not open Accessible Rescue
Holding both volume keys does not open the rescue. If your screen reader fails, that shortcut is how you get here without seeing the screen.
The volume shortcut has several features
With several features on the shortcut, Android asks which one to use, and that question is not spoken without a screen reader. Leave only Accessible Rescue on it.
Keep the volume shortcut for Accessible Rescue only
From the rescue you can turn your screen reader on and off, so you do not lose it.
Checked: the volume key shortcut opens only Accessible Rescue.
Accessibility settings open. Go into Accessible Rescue, turn on the Accessible Rescue shortcut and choose Hold volume keys. Remove the other features from that shortcut.
The shortcut does not work when the phone is locked
The volume key shortcut is off on the lock screen, which is exactly when it is needed most.
Allow the shortcut on the lock screen
Checked: the shortcut also works when the phone is locked.
Android will ask the first time you use the shortcut
The first time the volume shortcut is used, Android asks you to confirm. With the advanced permission it can be marked as answered.
Mark the shortcut question as answered
Checked: Android will not ask when you use the shortcut.
It could not be changed.
The guardian is off
The guardian warns you with the rescue voice if your screen reader or the system voice stop working, and opens the rescue with three quick presses of volume up.
Turn on the guardian
Accessible Rescue guardian
No advanced permission

With the advanced permission, the rescue turns screen readers on and changes the speech engine at once. Without it, it guides you through Settings. It is granted once from the app, in Advanced permission.
The phone language is %1$s
The phone is in %1$s. If someone changed it by mistake, your screen reader may speak that language or have no voice. The rescue voice stays in the language of this app.
Open language settings
To put your language back.
Language settings open. Put your language first in the list: drag it to the top or use its actions menu.
Battery optimization is on
These apps have battery optimization on: %1$s. On some phones the system closes them, and then the screen reader turns itself off.
Open battery optimization
Battery optimization open. Look for your screen reader, the speech engine and Accessible Rescue, and choose Don\'t optimize.
Open the manufacturer\'s autostart screen
Some manufacturers close apps even without battery optimization. There you allow them to keep running.
Manufacturer screen open. Allow autostart or background activity for your screen reader and Accessible Rescue.
Battery saver is on
With battery saver, some phones restrict apps in the background.
There is no backup of %1$s
A saved backup of %1$s lets you reinstall it with no Internet if it ever breaks. Make it while it works well.
Back up %1$s now
Backup done: %1$s, version %2$s.
There is not enough space for the backup.
There are no saved settings
Saving your settings while everything works lets you go back to them in one go. Save them only if everything works now.
Save the current settings
Do it only if your screen reader and the voice work well now.
Settings saved.
The settings could not be saved.

Puts the screen readers, speech engine and shortcuts back as they were.
This phone has no Play Store
Without Google\'s store, to reinstall TalkBack or the voice use the saved backups or an installation file. The rescue works the same.
Magnification is on
Magnification changes some gestures (triple tap). If you turned it on by mistake, turn it off.
Accessibility settings open. Look for Magnification and turn it off.
Color inversion is on
It only matters to someone who sees the screen: the colors are reversed.
Font size is at %1$d percent
